items.note: K1 gives the eight-row schedule, y_S <- y_S + x_S for arbitrary scratch, and the three-stage exchange (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) with restoration. K1.1-K1.4 follow the proof at 741-765: net change (JV+RG)x, the bit and complex central coefficients, and the three stages. The plan never states h=100, N, m or the wire counts W_b and W_c (767-782), but these are not part of the lemma's proof.

K2 states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, with one frame per gate and D_v D_u^{-1} on each edge. K2.1 gives the invariant and the R-linearity commutation (809-813). K2.2 gives the signed-route operator epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1} (818-825), exactly as in the paper.

The plan states the lemma's content: comparable labels, the only decreases on central 3->4 edges losing h, L=Ich, the sum Wm-2N+2L, the orthonormal bases over F_2, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. K3.1 attaches the pairing |S cap T|-1 to the F_2 dot product as well, but it holds only for the rational form I-J/9. The plan also omits the actual labels: the A, B, P, Q stage transitions, the terminal labels and the gate-label table eq:motif-labels (899-990). It also omits the per-edge residual table (1022-1043), so comparability is asserted rather than derived.

K4 states the projection assignment, the endpoint identity I_m and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m. The sub-steps follow the proof at 1156-1171: rank of P_V - P_U, the N source exceptions of rank one (2P_{U_a}), the deficit N - 2L_b, and the endpoint P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} = I_m. The shear frames Phi_M and the resulting H <- H+D on every role appear in K7.2.

K5 gives the phase frames, one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c < W_c m, and C^{otimes m} on every role. The sub-steps follow 1232-1314: mod-4 weight additivity, odd weight giving the two-point kernel, the deficit 2N-2L_c, and the X_a->Y_a correction by Z_{a,k}, i^{27k} and C = iZC^{-1}Z.

The plan gives L/N < 1/2 and both strict deficits. It gives the exact eta_b and eta_c, their comparison with 20*2^{-50}, log m < 20, m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-eta), and hence s/W < m^tau with tau = sigma = 1-2^{-50}. This is the paper's chain at 1319-1346.

S1 lists the four elementary operations correctly. S2 gives the split-and-swap idea for a controlled shift. However, its claim drops the hypothesis that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time (the quote contains it) and the prime-radix and denominator conditions. Neither step derives the unit multiplications or the counter analysis, so the item counts as stated, not derived.

The factorization A = E_1 Pi E_2 by top-row/rightmost-pivot elimination, triangular steps as controlled shifts, and the one-interchange realization of H_i <- H_i + D_j all follow 1375-1446. The plan never says that the shear acts over Z/q^b with a fixed odd prime q avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators (1397, 1413-1423). Without that, the rational factors are not known to specialize.

The plan follows the paper's proof step by step: cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on edges by rank-a shears, the frame identity giving Phi_{I_m}, merging to undo rho, the three-step interchange, s calls, and F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1) giving O(e^tau). It also covers the fixed-tape LIFO schedule at O(V) per node.

K7.5 states the O(Vu^tau) address permutation. The sub-steps reproduce 1650-1734: the top rho digits as the row field (R = q^{2rho} >= W^k), padding to R' < 2R, the base-m decomposition with the sum O(Ve^tau), and the binary-to-[q^e] padding. Unequal widths appear later in S8.1.11 and S9.3.8.

The plan follows 1806-1940. It gives the C identities, the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1} = X_{Mv} with columnwise P_M and one child per basis vector, the inverse child via (-i)^f Z C Z, the elimination count m(m-1)+3m, exactly s_c children on f = e/m axes, and H_0^{otimes D} = b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D.

The plan follows the proof at 2013-2207. It covers the eight conditional additions and their parity cycles, the guard interval 10 <= g <= 2^{K-1}-11, delta_bad = min{1, 80(f-1)2^{-K}} by a union bound, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, rotations as swap plus controlled shift (at most sixteen swaps and eight rotations), the radix-sort repair, and the final time with its o(1) extra terms.

The plan covers the individual-kernel cost O(Ve), the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), the q_0 row preprocessing and the u = Wg+w row split giving V/W children. It then gives the recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau+1) with F(e) = O(e) leaves, K <= e^{c/beta}, and the internal and leaf sums and base-m pieces leading to O(d^{lambda'}). All as in 2253-2448.

K8 and K8.5 state Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}, exact before one truncation. K8.4 reproduces the guard-width argument: A(e) <= sA(e/m) + E with E = 64(W+m+1)^3, A(e) <= 8B^2 d^{nu+1}, depth-l values in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] of modulus <= 2^l, and Delta = ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) = o(p) from epsilon*C_1 < 1. K8.5.2-K8.5.3 match the proof.

The plan covers character cancellation by the k -> k + t/2^{v+1} pairing, the decimation-in-frequency formula, bit-reversed storage B_t F_t^- with the reverse procedure F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, and grouping into a parallel H with monomial J_E. It then gives the layout L with prefix moves O(TpdK) and chunk exchanges O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), simultaneous rounds, J_E Q_p = Q_p J_E, the error sqrt2 l 2^{-p}, and the exact operators L B F^- and F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1}.

Each sub-step matches 3233-3367: B_0 = 2^{4p}, the evaluation bound, the separation |h_j| < B_0/2, the encoding carry in {-1,0}, the extraction carry in {0,1} with the residual identity, the final carry identity, negacyclic reduction |H_j| <= r 2^{2p}, truncation by a shift of p+l bits, and the cost dominated by four integer products.

S7.2 gives the normalization M F^+((F^-f)(F^-g)/r) = (f*g)/(rM) and P(LBu, LBv) = LB P(u,v). S7.3 gives the error chain 2delta, plus eta, 3delta + eta, times M = sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}. S7.4 gives the M = T/r products costing O(Tp log(rp)). All match 3414-3494.

The plan follows the paper's proof. It gives T P_s F_s = P_t F_t S, the bound on ||N-I||, the Neumann inverse, the normalizations 2^{-2alpha^2}, the error and time table, the ordered selector C, the choices of A-tilde and B_0-tilde, the retained (never executed) P_s and P_t, the tensor identity with gamma = 2d alpha^2, the linewise cost O(dTp^{3/2+delta} alpha) and the axis-exposure cost O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)).

S8.2 gives the chirp, its t_i-periodicity and the coefficient check for Q F_t. S8.3.1-S8.3.4 reproduce the unit-dilation identity F^+ R_c = R_c^{-1} F^+, R F^+ R = F^+, commutation with pointwise products, the normalization (u*v)/S^2, and the conjugation trick, as at 3939-3987.

The plan gives the fixed exponents, the sizes b, p, d, K and T, the r/2 and r axis split, the Rosser-Schoenfeld prime-interval count, distinct odd primes in ((1-2eta)t_i, (1-eta)t_i], T/2 < S < T by Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i > p, and an n^{o(1)} deterministic search, matching 4004-4179.

The plan covers the isomorphism via the order-S image of x, the triangular formula b_i and its proof, padding by a nested scan, update order i = d..1, rotation of the valid interval preserving zero padding, prefix-controlled shifts with o(Tp) offsets, and O(d^2) axis moves giving O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)). All follow 4204-4292.

The plan gives the chirp transform, the source transform F~ with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = R F_s, the opposite procedure (in S8.3.4), digit encoding a_j 2^{-b-2}, the six steps, and the explanation of the two occurrences of S. This is the paper's text at 4434-4544.

The error chain is reproduced exactly: E_ring < 5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s = 9 2^gamma TL, (2E_s+2), (3E_s+2), E_w < 28 2^gamma T^2 L, and the final bound below 1/2 via S <= T < 2^b, L < b and gamma small. The plan then gives uniqueness of rounding, the carry bound, the carry invariant and the 2n-bit output, matching 4557-4806.

The plan gives all seven table rows with their powers, the margins g_1 to g_7 with min = 2^{-181} = 2kappa, setup at o(Tp), exceptional sorting at o(V), log factors absorbed by p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff, as at 4815-4995.
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture. No step states what an eventual lower bound means, or that one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0 refutes it (381-387).

errors.says: For triple indicators <t_S,t_T> = |S cap T| - 1, with the form I-J/9 for the bit network and the dot product on F_2^h for the complex one (the formula attached to both).
errors.paper: The formula |S cap T| - 1 holds only for the rational form x^T(I-J/9)y (856-866). For the complex network the form is the ordinary F_2 dot product with t_T.t_T = 1, so t_S.t_T = |S cap T| mod 2 and neighbours (even intersection) are orthogonal (867-870). Under the plan's formula a triple would have norm 0 over F_2.

errors.says: Over F_2 every nonzero orthogonal residual is nonalternating because it contains a norm-one coordinate vector.
errors.paper: A norm-one vector in each residual is built by tensoring chosen norm-one vectors in each factor. Some are coordinate units, but the lines P and Q are spanned by triple-indicator tensors, so some residuals, such as the line P (x) <t_Y> (x) Q, contain no coordinate vector (1073-1085).

errors.says: Both tape procedures cost F_k = O(e^tau) per unit volume with tau < 1.
errors.paper: Only the interchange satisfies F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1), hence O(e^tau) (1550-1557). The butterfly layer has node overhead O((eK)^tau + 1) and leaf cost O(e), with total O(d^{lambda'}) where lambda' = 1-2^{-54} > tau (2406-2445).

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from start to finish. It builds the two exchange networks, frames, labels and rational and phase interfaces (K1-K5), and the exponent tau = 1-2^{-50} (K6). From these it gets the O(Vu^tau) interchange (K7) and the O(Vd^{lambda'}) butterfly layer (K8), then synthetic transforms and convolution (S6-S7), resampling, chirp and permutation cancellation (S8), and parameters, assembly, exact recovery and the cost table (S9-S10), ending at O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It is thin in two places. The label construction is asserted rather than derived: the stage labels, terminal labels and residual table are missing, and the F_2 pairing is mislabelled. The concrete sizes h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 behind the ratios 100/539 and m < 2^20 are never stated.

steps.note: K1 carries the fixed linear network on triples: eight rows, y_S <- y_S + x_S for arbitrary scratch, and three stages giving (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored. This is the network in its role. The explicit sizes h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3, and the indexing a in T^3, are not stated. The verdict leans on the fully given mechanism.

K2 and K2.1 state that a common invertible frame commutes with a pointwise gate, that the array network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and that each edge pays only D_v D_u^{-1}, so the intermediate frames are free.

K3 and K3.2 give nested nondegenerate subspaces of F^{(x)3} from triple indicators, every edge comparable, and the only decreases on central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing dimension h. The explicit label table is omitted, and K3.1 misstates the F_2 pairing.
K4.1 states that P_V - P_U has rank dim V - dim U for nested nondegenerate U in V. K4.2 states that the N negative source projections are the exceptions, each edge 2P_{U_a} of rank one.
K3.3 gives L = Ich and the sum of |Delta dim| = Wm - 2N + 2L by telescoping at gates. K4.3 gives s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b.
K3.5 gives L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539, both below 1/2. K4.3 and K5.3 give the positive deficits N - 2L_b and 2N - 2L_c, so s < Wm.
K4.4 gives M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m for every role, with P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} = I_m. K7.2.3 shows that the shear frames then give H <- H+D on every row, scratch rows included.

K7.1 gives a rank-a shear via A = E_1 Pi E_2 at exactly a interchanges plus O(V). K7.2.2 performs each edge Phi_{A_e} this way, with the pivot interchanges as recursive calls. K7.4.1 says the total is exactly s calls. The fixed prime q is not mentioned.

K7.2.1 gives children of volume V/W, and K7.4.2 gives F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1). K6 derives s/W < m^tau with tau = 1-2^{-50} from eta > 20*2^{-50} and log m < 20. K7.4.3-K7.4.4 conclude F_k = O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan rebuilds the whole central-saving chain in order. The network (K1) gets frames (K2) and nested labels (K3). Ranks equal dimension changes except for the N source edges (K4.1-K4.2), which gives the budget s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b (K3.3, K4.3). The ratios L/N = 100/539 and 101/539 below 1/2 give s < Wm (K3.5). The endpoint identity yields H <- H+D (K4.4, K7.2.3), each edge becomes rank-many interchanges (K7.1), and the recurrence with s/W < m^{1-2^{-50}} gives F_k = O(e^tau) (K6, K7.4). It is thin at the start: h=100, N and m are never given explicitly, the label table is only asserted, and the F_2 pairing is misstated.
